title: Exchange symmetry, Schur–Weyl and Temperley–Lieb spin algebra

items.title: Finite spin-half tensor chains
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $N\geq1$ be an integer. The finite spin-half tensor chain is the complex
inner-product space
$$\mathcal H_N:=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes N}$$
with the standard tensor-product inner product, linear in its first argument.
Fix the standard orthonormal basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$ of $\mathbb C^2$.
Let $\sigma^x,\sigma^y,\sigma^z$ be the Pauli matrices of the finite-spin
matrix supplier, and for $1\leq k\leq N$ define
$$\sigma_k^a:=I^{\otimes(k-1)}\otimes\sigma^a\otimes I^{\otimes(N-k)},\qquad J_k^a:=\tfrac12\sigma_k^a\quad(a\in\{x,y,z\}).$$
For $1\leq i<N$, define the adjacent swap $s_i$ on elementary tensors by
$$s_i(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_N):=v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{i+1}\otimes v_i\otimes\cdots\otimes v_N.$$
Write
$$|\omega\rangle:=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}(|0\rangle\otimes|1\rangle-|1\rangle\otimes|0\rangle),\qquad P_i:=I^{\otimes(i-1)}\otimes P_\omega\otimes I^{\otimes(N-i-1)},$$
where $P_\omega v:=\langle v,\omega\rangle\,\omega$ on the adjacent two
factors. Also put $e_i:=I_{\mathcal H_N}-s_i$ for $1\leq i<N$. If $N=1$,
these bond-indexed families are empty.

This is a mathematical definition of finite-dimensional tensor spaces and
operators; it makes no physical claim about a material, a particle species, or
an adopted statistics sector.

references.title: Yacine Ikhlef, Jesper Lykke Jacobsen, and Hubert Saleur, A Temperley-Lieb quantum chain with two- and three-site interactions, section 2

items.title: The collision-free unordered configuration space of two planar points
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Give $\mathbb R^4$ its Euclidean topology, whose basic open sets are the
Euclidean open balls, and write a point as an ordered pair $(x,y)$ with
$x,y\in\mathbb R^2$. The **ordered configuration space** is the subspace
$$F_2(\mathbb R^2):=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb R^2:x\ne y\}$$
with the subspace topology. The transposition acts by $(x,y)\mapsto(y,x)$.
The **unordered configuration space of two distinct planar points** is
$$C_2(\mathbb R^2):=F_2(\mathbb R^2)/\bigl((x,y)\sim(y,x)\bigr)$$
with the quotient topology of the canonical projection
$q:F_2(\mathbb R^2)\to C_2(\mathbb R^2)$. We write its points as unordered
sets $\{x,y\}$; equality in this set means equality up to transposition.
The diagonal $x=y$ is excluded, so collisions are not points of this space.

The topology on each finite Cartesian coordinate space used below is its
Euclidean topology; on a finite product it is equivalently the topology with
basis the products of open sets in the factors.

references.title: Chetan Nayak, Steven H. Simon, Ady Stern, Michael Freedman, and Sankar Das Sarma, Non-Abelian Anyons and Topological Quantum Computation, §II.A.1

items.title: The real-form star involution on the loop-weight-two Temperley–Lieb algebra
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
For each integer $N\geq0$, let $P_N(\mathbb C,2)$ be the quotient of the free
unital associative complex algebra on $u_1,\ldots,u_{N-1}$ by the relations
$$u_i^2=2u_i,\qquad u_iu_j=u_ju_i\ (|i-j|>1),\qquad u_iu_{i+1}u_i=u_i,\quad u_{i+1}u_iu_{i+1}=u_{i+1}.$$
This complex Temperley–Lieb algebra has a
conjugate-linear anti-involution $*$ determined by
$$c^*=\overline c\quad(c\in\mathbb C),\qquad u_i^*=u_i\quad(1\leq i<N),\qquad (xy)^*=y^*x^*.$$
For $N=0$ or $N=1$ this is complex conjugation on $\mathbb C$.

references.title: David Ridout and Yvan Saint-Aubin, Standard Modules, Induction and the Structure of the Temperley–Lieb Algebra, §2

items.title: Unitary exchange blocks for collective spins
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $d\geq1$ and $N\geq0$ be integers, let $V=\mathbb C^d$ with its standard
Hermitian inner product, and give $H_N:=V^{\otimes N}$ its standard
tensor-product inner product. For $\pi\in S_N$ use the left place action
$$\rho(\pi)(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_N):=v_{\pi^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\pi^{-1}(N)},$$
and for $U\in U(d):=\{A\in M_d(\mathbb C):A^*A=I\}$ use the diagonal action
$\Delta_N(U):=U^{\otimes N}$. For a partition $\lambda\vdash N$ with at most
$d$ rows, let $S^\lambda$ be the corresponding complex Specht module and put
$$M_\lambda:=\operatorname{Hom}_{S_N}(S^\lambda,H_N),\qquad d_\lambda:=\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\lambda.$$
Equip $S^\lambda$ with any $S_N$-invariant Hermitian inner product and equip
$M_\lambda$ with the normalized Hilbert-Schmidt inner product
$$\langle f,g\rangle_{M_\lambda}:=d_\lambda^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}(g^*f).$$
Equip each $S^\lambda\otimes M_\lambda$ with the product inner product,
defined on elementary tensors by
$\langle s\otimes f,s'\otimes g\rangle=
\langle s,s'\rangle\langle f,g\rangle$ and extended sesquilinearly, and give
the direct sum the orthogonal direct-sum inner product.
Then the evaluation map
$$\Phi:\bigoplus_{\lambda\vdash N,\ \ell(\lambda)\leq d}S^\lambda\otimes M_\lambda\longrightarrow H_N,\qquad \Phi(s\otimes f):=f(s),$$
is unitary. Under this decomposition every permutation acts on $S^\lambda$
and as the identity on $M_\lambda$, while every diagonal $U(d)$ action acts
as the identity on $S^\lambda$ and by postcomposition on $M_\lambda$. The
multiplicity spaces in the sum are nonzero; partitions with more than $d$
rows have zero multiplicity space.

references.title: Representation Theory, CT, Lent 2005, sections 23.14–24.9, complete course notes
Caroline Gruson and Vera Serganova, A Sentimental Journey through Representation Theory: from Finite Groups to Quivers (via Algebras), chapter 6 section 2.2

items.title: The planar two-point configuration space retracts to the quotient circle
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $q_0:=\{(1,0),(-1,0)\}\in C_2(\mathbb R^2)$. There is a pointed
homeomorphism
$$\bigl(C_2(\mathbb R^2),q_0\bigr)\cong \bigl(\mathbb R^2\times(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R/\mathbb Z, (0,1,[0])\bigr),$$
and
$$\pi_1(C_2(\mathbb R^2),q_0)\cong(\mathbb Z,+).$$
Under the isomorphism specified in the proof, the counterclockwise exchange
loop
$$\gamma(t):=\{(\cos\pi t,\sin\pi t),(-\cos\pi t,-\sin\pi t)\},\qquad 0\leq t\leq1,$$
is a positive generator. The loop in which the relative direction makes one
full counterclockwise turn is $[\gamma]^2$, so it represents twice the
generator.

references.title: Chetan Nayak, Steven H. Simon, Ady Stern, Michael Freedman, and Sankar Das Sarma, Non-Abelian Anyons and Topological Quantum Computation, §II.A.1

items.title: Spin-half swaps realize the Temperley–Lieb algebra at loop weight two
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $N\geq1$, $\mathcal H_N=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes N}$ with the standard
orthonormal basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$ on each factor, and for
$1\leq i<N$ define $s_i$ to swap factors $i,i+1$. Put
$|\omega\rangle=(|01\rangle-|10\rangle)/\sqrt2$,
$P_\omega v=\langle v,\omega\rangle\omega$, let $P_i$ act as $P_\omega$ on
factors $i,i+1$ and identity on all others, and set $e_i=I-s_i$. For every
bond,
$$e_i=I-s_i=2P_i,\qquad e_i^*=e_i,\qquad e_i^2=2e_i.$$
For $1\leq i<N-1$,
$$e_i e_{i+1}e_i=e_i,\qquad e_{i+1}e_i e_{i+1}=e_{i+1},$$
and $e_i e_j=e_j e_i$ when $|i-j|>1$. Consequently the assignment
$u_i\mapsto e_i$ defines a star-preserving algebra representation
$$P_N(\mathbb C,2)\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H_N).$$
For $\lambda\vdash N$ with at most two rows, put
$M_\lambda=\operatorname{Hom}_{S_N}(S^\lambda,\mathcal H_N)$ and use the
unitary Schur–Weyl decomposition
$\mathcal H_N\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda\vdash N,\,\ell(\lambda)\le2}
S^\lambda\otimes M_\lambda$. Each $e_i$ acts on the Specht factor as
$I-\rho_\lambda((i,i+1))$ and as identity on the multiplicity factor. No
faithfulness assertion is made.

references.title: Yacine Ikhlef, Jesper Lykke Jacobsen, and Hubert Saleur, A Temperley–Lieb quantum chain with two- and three-site interactions, §2

items.title: The finite isotropic spin-half exchange Hamiltonian is a Temperley–Lieb element
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $N\geq1$, let $\hbar>0$, and let real couplings
$\mathcal J_i\in\mathbb R$ be given for $1\leq i<N$. On
$\mathcal H_N=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes N}$, let $\sigma_i^a$ be the Pauli
matrix $\sigma^a$ acting on factor $i$ and identity on all other factors,
where
$$\sigma^x=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad \sigma^y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\quad \sigma^z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$
Let $s_i$ swap factors $i,i+1$ and put $e_i=I-s_i$. Set
$S_i^a:=\hbar\sigma_i^a/2$ for $a\in\{x,y,z\}$, and define the finite-chain
operator
$$H:=\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\mathcal J_i\hbar^{-2}\sum_{a=x,y,z}S_i^aS_{i+1}^a.$$
For every bond,
$$\hbar^{-2}\sum_a S_i^aS_{i+1}^a=\tfrac12s_i-\tfrac14I =\tfrac14I-\tfrac12e_i.$$
Thus $H=\sum_i\mathcal J_i(\tfrac14I-\tfrac12e_i)$ is self-adjoint, belongs
to the represented Temperley–Lieb algebra, and on each summand of the unitary
decomposition
$$\mathcal H_N\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda\vdash N,\,\ell(\lambda)\le2} S^\lambda\otimes M_\lambda,\qquad M_\lambda:=\operatorname{Hom}_{S_N}(S^\lambda,\mathcal H_N),$$
acts on $S^\lambda$ and as identity on $M_\lambda$. For $N=1$ the sum is
empty and $H=0$.

references.title: Yacine Ikhlef, Jesper Lykke Jacobsen, and Hubert Saleur, A Temperley–Lieb quantum chain with two- and three-site interactions, Introduction and §2

items.title: The quotient line bundle associated with a planar exchange character
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Use the pointed coordinate identification
$$C_2(\mathbb R^2)\cong\mathbb R^2\times(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R/\mathbb Z,$$
which sends $q_0=\{(1,0),(-1,0)\}$ to $(0,1,[0])$, to write
$$X:=C_2(\mathbb R^2)\cong\mathbb R^2\times(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R/\mathbb Z.$$
Put $\widetilde X:=\mathbb R^2\times(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ and define
$$p(c,\rho,t):=(c,\rho,[t])\in X,\qquad T_n(c,\rho,t):=(c,\rho,t+n)\quad(n\in\mathbb Z).$$
Define $U(1):=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ under complex multiplication. Let
$\chi:\mathbb Z\to U(1)$ satisfy
$\chi(0)=1$ and $\chi(m+n)=\chi(m)\chi(n)$ for all $m,n\in\mathbb Z$.
Let $\mathbb Z$ act on
$\widetilde X\times\mathbb C$ by
$$n\cdot((c,\rho,t),z):=((c,\rho,t+n),\chi(n)^{-1}z).$$
The homomorphism law for $\chi$ makes this a group action, and its orbits
define the quotient relation.
Define the **character quotient** and its projection by
$$L_\chi:=(\widetilde X\times\mathbb C)/\mathbb Z, \qquad \Pi_\chi([\widetilde x,z]):=p(\widetilde x),$$
with the quotient topology on $L_\chi$. Since $p(T_n\widetilde x)=p(\widetilde x)$,
it induces a continuous map $\Pi_\chi:L_\chi\to X$. Once $p$ is known to be
a covering map, the **monodromy** of this quotient around a based loop means
the fiber map obtained by lifting the loop and keeping its complex coordinate
$z$ constant along the lift.

For this item, a **unitary flat complex line bundle** over a space $X$ means a
continuous surjection $\Pi:L\to X$ with local trivializations
$\Pi^{-1}(U)\cong U\times\mathbb C$ over open sets $U$, whose changes of fiber
coordinate on overlaps are multiplication by functions $g:U\cap V\to U(1)$
that are locally constant (constant on some neighbourhood of each point).
The definition above names the quotient data; the following theorem verifies
that $L_\chi$ has these line-bundle and flatness properties.

references.title: Chetan Nayak, Steven H. Simon, Ady Stern, Michael Freedman, and Sankar Das Sarma, Non-Abelian Anyons and Topological Quantum Computation, §II.A.1

items.title: The planar exchange character quotient is a flat unitary line bundle
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
For every character $\chi:\mathbb Z\to U(1)$, the coordinate covering
$p:\widetilde X\to X$ and quotient $\Pi_\chi:L_\chi\to X$ defined by the
character-quotient construction have the following properties:

1. $p$ is a universal covering map and its deck transformations are exactly
   $T_n(c,\rho,t)=(c,\rho,t+n)$, $n\in\mathbb Z$.
2. $\Pi_\chi$ is a unitary flat complex line bundle, meaning its local
   transition phases are locally constant.
3. Parallel transport defined by keeping the lifted fiber coordinate fixed
   has monodromy $\chi(n)$ on a based loop whose lift ends at $T_n\widetilde x$.

In particular, a positive planar exchange has monodromy $\chi(1)$ and a full
relative winding has monodromy $\chi(2)$.

references.title: Chetan Nayak, Steven H. Simon, Ady Stern, Michael Freedman, and Sankar Das Sarma, Non-Abelian Anyons and Topological Quantum Computation, §II.A.1

items.title: Planar two-particle exchange characters and the full-winding phase
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $C_2(\mathbb R^2)$ be the quotient space of two ordered distinct points
in $\mathbb R^2$ by transposition, with basepoint
$q_0=\{(1,0),(-1,0)\}$. A **one-dimensional unitary character** means a group homomorphism
$$\chi:\pi_1(C_2(\mathbb R^2),q_0)\longrightarrow U(1),$$
where $U(1)$ is the multiplicative group of complex numbers of modulus one.
For every such character there is a unique angle modulo $2\pi$ with
$$\chi(n[\gamma])=e^{in\theta}:=\cos(n\theta)+i\sin(n\theta),\qquad n\in\mathbb Z,$$
where $\gamma(t)=\{(\cos\pi t,\sin\pi t),(-\cos\pi t,-\sin\pi t)\}$
is the counterclockwise exchange path and $[\gamma]$ its positive generator.
A full
counterclockwise turn of the relative direction is $2[\gamma]$ and has phase
$e^{2i\theta}$. The character factors through the permutation group
$S_2\cong\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ exactly when $\theta\equiv0$ or $\pi$
modulo $2\pi$; these are the symmetric and antisymmetric exchange characters.
Both sectors occur in $(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes2}$, but this theorem makes no
physical choice between them. The associated quotient $L_{\chi_\theta}$ is a
flat unitary complex line bundle whose monodromy is $e^{i\theta}$ around the
positive exchange and $e^{2i\theta}$ around a full relative winding.

references.title: Chetan Nayak, Steven H. Simon, Ady Stern, Michael Freedman, and Sankar Das Sarma, Non-Abelian Anyons and Topological Quantum Computation, §II.A.1

title: Exchange symmetry, Schur–Weyl and Temperley–Lieb spin algebra — Examples

items.title: Permutation invariance alone does not select a statistics sector
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
The false claim is: if a linear operator on
$H_2=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes2}$ commutes with the transposition that swaps the
two tensor factors, then the whole space $H_2$ must lie in one exchange
eigenspace, either the symmetric $+1$ eigenspace or the antisymmetric $-1$
eigenspace. More generally, the claim that permutation invariance by itself
chooses one of those two sectors is false.

references.title: Chetan Nayak, Steven H. Simon, Ady Stern, Michael Freedman, and Sankar Das Sarma, Non-Abelian Anyons and Topological Quantum Computation, §II.A.1

items.title: Three spin-half factors: the quartet and the two exchange-coupled doublets
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Use the standard Pauli matrices
$$\sigma^x=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad \sigma^y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\quad \sigma^z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},$$
and let $\sigma_j^a$ act by $\sigma^a$ on tensor factor $j$ and identity on
the other factors. Let $|abc\rangle:=|a\rangle\otimes|b\rangle\otimes|c\rangle$ for
$a,b,c\in\{0,1\}$. In $\mathcal H_3=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes3}$ define
$$\begin{aligned} q_{3/2}&=|000\rangle,& q_{1/2}&=(|100\rangle+|010\rangle+|001\rangle)/\sqrt3,\\ q_{-1/2}&=(|110\rangle+|101\rangle+|011\rangle)/\sqrt3,& q_{-3/2}&=|111\rangle,\\ a_+&=(|010\rangle-|100\rangle)/\sqrt2,& a_-&=(|011\rangle-|101\rangle)/\sqrt2,\\ b_+&=(2|001\rangle-|010\rangle-|100\rangle)/\sqrt6,& b_-&=(|101\rangle+|011\rangle-2|110\rangle)/\sqrt6. \end{aligned}$$
These eight vectors form an orthonormal basis. With
$K_z:=\tfrac12\sum_{j=1}^3\sigma_j^z$ and
$K_+:=\tfrac12\sum_{j=1}^3(\sigma_j^x+i\sigma_j^y)$, the $q$-vectors form
the spin-$3/2$ ladder and the $a$- and $b$-pairs form two spin-$1/2$ ladders.
For $K_-:=\tfrac12\sum_{j=1}^3(\sigma_j^x-i\sigma_j^y)$, their lowering
actions are the adjoints of the raising actions displayed below:
$$K_+q_{1/2}=\sqrt3q_{3/2},\quad K_+q_{-1/2}=2q_{1/2},\quad K_+q_{-3/2}=\sqrt3q_{-1/2},\qquad K_+a_-=a_+,\quad K_+b_-=b_+,$$
with the highest vectors killed by $K_+$ and the stated subscripts giving the
$K_z$ eigenvalues. The adjacent swaps act as identity on the quartet and on
each magnetic pair $(a_+,b_+)$ and $(a_-,b_-)$ by
$$s_{12}=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad s_{23}=\begin{pmatrix}1/2&\sqrt3/2\\\sqrt3/2&-1/2\end{pmatrix}.$$
For $\hbar>0$, set $S_j^a=\hbar\sigma_j^a/2$, and for real couplings
$\mathcal J_{12},\mathcal J_{23}$ define
$$H_3:=\sum_{j=1}^{2}\mathcal J_{j,j+1}\hbar^{-2} \sum_{a=x,y,z}S_j^aS_{j+1}^a.$$
This finite-chain exchange operator is the scalar
$(\mathcal J_{12}+\mathcal J_{23})/4$ on the quartet and, on
each doublet multiplicity basis $(a_\pm,b_\pm)$, has matrix
$$\frac14\begin{pmatrix}-3\mathcal J_{12}&\sqrt3\mathcal J_{23}\\ \sqrt3\mathcal J_{23}&\mathcal J_{12}-2\mathcal J_{23}\end{pmatrix}.$$
The latter matrix has eigenvalues
$$-\frac{\mathcal J_{12}+\mathcal J_{23}}4\ \pm\ \frac12\sqrt{\mathcal J_{12}^2-\mathcal J_{12}\mathcal J_{23}+ \mathcal J_{23}^2},$$
each repeated for the two magnetic states.
